Next week totals 45 miles (6+10+6+5+18), which is a sensible step from 40 and below the 53-mile peak. It keeps her five-day pattern (rest Monday and Friday, the session on Wednesday, the long run on Sunday), and each day is clear enough to run as written.

What lowers the score is invented detail. Nothing on the card says she hit every session, that her marathon-pace work landed on 8:35/mi, or that the race is five weeks away. The answer to her question rests on that made-up race timing. It also never responds to her club mate's 70 miles, and it doesn't mention her heavy legs early in the week.

The plan is also heavy. It has two big marathon-pace efforts: 7 miles at 8:35 on Wednesday, then an 18-mile long run finishing with 6 miles at 8:35. The 18 miles is about 40% of the week. We don't know her recent long runs, so I can't call this a sharp jump, but it's an aggressive mix. The opening line ("push the long run back…") is also unclear. Overall the answer is safe and useful, but the read of her week isn't drawn from what she actually reported.

── MARISOL'S WEEK ──
Marisol is training for a second marathon, the Wexley Lakes Marathon, aiming to break 3:45 after a 4:02 debut. Marisol runs five days a week, with a session on Wednesday, the long run on Sunday and Monday and Friday off, and ran about 30 miles a week before this build.
Recent weeks: 24, 27, 37, 53 mi
This week: 40 mi over 5 runs.
Body: "Legs a bit heavy early in the week, fine by Thursday."
Asks: "My club mate runs 70 miles a week before a marathon. I'm thinking of doubling to 80 next week to catch up, running twice a day. Would that work?"

── THE DRAFT ──
Tells Marisol: You hit every session as planned and the marathon-pace work landed right on 8:35/mi, so we stay the course and push the long run back…
Answers: No, please do not double to 80 miles next week. Five weeks out from the race is the worst possible moment to jump from 40 to 80; the single biggest predictor of a bad marathon is a sudden spike in load in the final month.
Next week:
Mon: rest. Full day off after the long run to absorb the work.
Tue: easy, 6 mi, heart rate under 145, flat route. Loosens the legs and keeps it truly…
Wed: quality, 10 mi with 2 mi warm-up, 7 mi at 8:35/mi, 1 mi cool-down. Rehearses goal…
Thu: easy, 6 mi, heart rate under 145. Recovery day; keep it conversational.
Fri: rest. Keep it a real rest day before the weekend work.
Sat: easy, 5 mi, heart rate under 145, add 4 x 20 sec strides at the end. Strides wake…
Sun: long, 18 mi, first 12 mi easy under 150 bpm then last 6 mi at 8:35/mi. Builds…
